title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression gating + CI eval integration
author: Avery Kim
description:
Motivation: We need automated, deterministic checks that detect regressions in quality from prompt set changes and model rollouts. This PR adds a prompt-set regression gating layer to the eval-harness, exposes a lightweight gating config, and hooks it into CI so that PRs touching prompt sets or model config can block merges when quality drops below configured thresholds.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a prompt_regression module that computes delta metrics (accuracy, BLEU, rougeL, custom scoring) between a baseline and candidate run and evaluates against per-prompt-set thresholds.
- Introduces a gating config format (yaml) that lives next to prompt-sets and supports percent-delta and absolute thresholds, per-metric exemptions, and an allowlist for experimental models.
- Adds a CI job (ci/eval_prompt_gate.yml) that runs a fast eval (sampled prompts, cached model outputs when available) and posts a status and human-readable artifact with the diff.
- Integrates gating decisions into PR status: failing gate blocks merge and comments the failure summary; passing gate adds an informational status and artifact link.
- Adds unit and integration tests for core gating logic and a smoke test for the CI job.

Checklist: [x] gating logic implemented; [x] config parser + schema; [x] CI job; [x] tests; [x] docs/README for teams; [x] rollout plan (gradual, opt-in by default).

Constraints/Design notes: The gate runs a sampled eval (default 250 prompts) to keep runtime < 10m on CI. Full evals remain available as artifacts. Gate thresholds are conservative and can be overridden via Linear ticket. This is opt-in: repo teams must enable a .eval-gate.yaml file to turn on blocking semantics.

Related: Linear ENG-7123 (prompt-regression initiative), ENG-7268 (CI integration spike). See internal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-7123/prompt-set-regression-gating for rationale and examples.

Merge strategy: squash merge after approvals and green CI. Rollout: opt-in for redwood repo teams; will enable for eval-harness and redwood-model-registry in phased rollout.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on gating semantics (percent vs absolute), performance of the sampled runner, and CI artifact usability. The diff includes small, self-contained changes in several modules and a new CI workflow.

review_comments: Diego Martinez (review): Can we make the sampled prompt set size configurable per-gate? Right now 250 is hardcoded in runner.py — suggest pulling from config with safe upper bound.
Author (Avery Kim): Updated to read sample_size from .eval-gate.yaml with max cap of 1000. Default remains 250. See commit d4e5f6a.
Priya Shah (review): Need clearer signal in the CI artifact about which prompts caused the largest deltas. Suggest top-10 contributors table.

Author (Avery Kim): Added top_k_contributors table to the artifact and linked in PR comment. Also added an optional 'explain' flag to produce per-prompt diffs in artifacts (disabled by default on CI to save time).
Liam O'Connor (approve): LGTM after addressing sample_size and artifact clarity. Approving for merge.
release_notes: Adds opt-in prompt-set regression gating to eval-harness with CI integration. Teams can enable gating via .eval-gate.yaml next to prompt sets; CI job will run a sampled eval and block merges on regressions. Includes docs and rollout guidance.
